concern_details.detail: main architectural components and their responsibilities
concern_details.why: Seven components, one per role. Each has a one-line responsibility in the diagram: GUI screens, the services facade as GUI entry point, one controller per use case, report and user services holding the business rules and returning Maps, domain entities, generic persistence service, and external MySQL. They match the code. The facade could also say that it turns exceptions into boolean results (SystemServicesController), but an architect does not need that to plan evolution.

The four Java packages Boundary, Control, Entity and Database are drawn as containers. ReportService and UserService sit visibly inside the Entity package, which matches the code (Entity/ReportService.java, Entity/UserService.java). MySQL is outside every package.

Every drawn dependency is backed by an import or instantiation. GUIs use SystemServicesController. UserLoginGUI:111 creates UserLoginController directly, which is the bypass. The facade creates seven controllers (SystemServicesController:23-29). All controllers create ReportService and/or UserService. Both services create PersistenceService. ReportCreationGUI, ReceivedReportsGUI and ReportCreationController import Entity.ReportCategory. No Entity or Database class imports Boundary or Control, so no dependency is missing or reversed.

concern_details.detail: separation of user interface, application logic, domain entities and persistence, and how they collaborate
concern_details.why: The view shows the separation: the GUI never reaches persistence, and the only entity leaks to the GUI and controllers are the ReportCategory enum. It also shows how the layers collaborate: data crosses layers as Map<String,Object>, which the facade's signatures confirm. The note on the services states the main separation weakness: the Entity package depends on Database, so the domain is not persistence-ignorant.

level_why: Seven components plus four layer packages and one interface suit an architect who wants the whole system before planning its evolution. Classes are merged by role: ten GUIs, nine controllers, the entity and state classes, and PersistenceService with JpaUtil. Separating the facade from the controllers is justified by the login bypass. Nothing should be dropped. Splitting further, for example into individual controllers or the Report state classes, would be too detailed.
unsupported: The 'Services API' interface has no Java interface in the code. It stands for the public method set of the concrete class SystemServicesController. The README states this assumption, but the diagram shows it as if it were a declared interface. This is acceptable as a logical provided interface, but a note or label would make the source clear.
uml: The Entity package is still titled 'domain and domain services', and the note says 'Domain services depend on persistence'. The README says the 'domain services' wording was dropped. Use one name for ReportService/UserService ('report and user services') everywhere so the layer naming is consistent.

'persist ..> model : mapped by config' is a plain dependency with no stereotype, while every other dependency is «use». That is valid UML, and the label correctly says it comes from persistence.xml and not from code. Optionally mark it with a short note so it does not read as a code dependency.

MySQL is a plain component that says 'external system' in its name. No standard stereotype is needed, but placing it outside a drawn system boundary would make 'external' a model fact rather than text. This is minor.
fixes: Use one name for ReportService/UserService in the Entity package title and the persistence note (for example 'report and user services'), and drop 'domain services'.
Mark the 'Services API' interface as the public operations of SystemServicesController (no Java interface exists), for example with a short label or note.
Optionally add 'turns exceptions into boolean results' to the facade's responsibility line.
